target_claim_or_section: minutesPerTouch: exceptionNoAi = nativeD / f; doc 10 §6 'at pessimistic 0.9 the AI step is worth about $4'
challenge: The AI factor is applied backwards. Native (MD-5) minutes are fixed inputs taken from the activity register's AI-native column, and the no-AI counterfactual (MD-4) is derived as native/f. Lowering AI efficacy therefore makes MD-4 cheaper and leaves MD-5 unchanged: the AI-native mode's own cost and break-even cannot respond to the AI evidence. The '~10% from AI' and '$4 at 0.9' figures re-label savings and do not stress-test them. ai_assist_duration_factor is not in the MD-5 tornado at all.
evidence: Scratch rerun f=0.88 as the docs do: MD-5 stays at 26.0 min, $85 variable, $1.46B break-even; the AI share falls to 1.2% and the 'saving' moves to 'exception-only design' (+$18). If native minutes are scaled honestly (duration_mult_native=f/0.6): f=0.88 gives MD-5 38.1 min, $98 variable, $1.51B break-even (P50 $1.77B); f=0.97 gives 42.0 min, $102 variable, $1.53B, and the AI step is about -$0.2/acct.
proposed_change: Anchor the MD-4 (no-AI) minutes as inputs and derive MD-5 = MD-4 × f, so the AI factor flows into MD-5 cost, the tornado and the Monte Carlo. Restate CLM-011 as conditional on f.

target_claim_or_section: §6 and PAR-007: AI cuts minutes per touch by 40% (0.6; range 0.4-0.9)
challenge: The base 0.6 equals the most favourable lab result (Noy & Zhang 2023: about 40% time saved on short, stylized writing tasks) and better than BCG's inside-frontier result (Dell'Acqua et al. 2023: 25% faster). Field evidence is much smaller. In customer support, Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond find about 14% more resolutions per hour (f≈0.88), concentrated among novices, with little gain for experienced agents. The residual exceptions here are worked by compliance and accounting specialists, exactly where those gains vanish. Humlum & Vestergaard's Danish administrative data show about 3% of work hours saved and precise-zero earnings and hours effects. The low end of 0.4 has no empirical support.
evidence: Literature as cited. f=0.88 (honest propagation): AI step $4.1/acct instead of $17.5; MD-5 human minutes 26→38 (+47%).
proposed_change: Set base f to 0.85-0.9 and range to 0.75-1.0. Treat 0.6 as an upside case to be shown by the V-7 time study (OQ-011).

target_claim_or_section: EV-E08, EV-E10, EV-E04, EV-E13 native touch probabilities and prevention efficacies
challenge: Prevention appears to be double counted. EV-E08's native touch rate (0.0117) is already based on 'change-driven vetting central estimate ~5 reviews per 1000 grants', and the same change-driven monitoring is then applied again as prevention (efficacy 0.5). EV-E10's native touch rate of 0.09 is calibrated to a replay proxy (7.4-11.2% routed) that presumably already applies policy rules, and 'pre-validated policy rules' then remove another 40%. EV-E13 and EV-E04 follow the same pattern. So the $33.5 'prevention' step is partly a second application of the redesign already priced into the native touch rates.
evidence: Scratch rerun with prevention zeroed for E08/E10/E13 and E04 cut 0.6→0.3: MD-5 rises 26.0→36.2 min and $85→$101 variable; break-even $1.46B→$1.53B (P50 $1.74B→$1.81B); the prevention step falls from $33.5 to $9.9.
proposed_change: For each event, state whether the native-touch basis is measured before or after the prevention mechanism. Apply prevention only to pre-mechanism rates.

challenge: The 'deterministic workflow' step takes MD-3's structured-event touch rates directly from the AI-native activity column (E03 0.60→0.03; E08 0.37→0.0117; E13 0.05→0.01; E20 0.016→0.0009). Nothing shows these rates come from rules and not from AI classification or extraction, such as check and remittance parsing or purpose matching. The 97% straight-through rate assumed for contribution posting covers checks and securities. Ops benchmarks for mature payment and securities processing only approach that level after years of tuning; it is not an entry-year rate. The decomposition is order-dependent and fragile. With touch rates ×1.5 and durations ×1.3, the 'exception-only design' step turns negative (-$20/acct), because MD-4's derived minutes (native/0.6, e.g. E10 42 min vs 12.4 conventional) exceed the conventional ones.
evidence: events.csv basis column cites ACT ai_native values. Tornado touch_mult_native=2 → $1.56B. Scratch rerun touch×1.5 and duration×1.3: MD-5 48.7 min, $111 variable, $1.56B; decomposition MD-3→MD-4 = -$20.2.
proposed_change: Label MD-3 touch rates as unmeasured ramp-year targets. Use an entry-year touch multiplier of 1.5-2.0 that falls with volume (learning curve). Report Shapley-averaged attribution over step orderings, not one sequential path.

target_claim_or_section: MD-5 fixed = MD-4 + ~$0.1M 'AI evaluation and governance'
challenge: Induced work from AI is underpriced. $0.1M does not cover model risk management of the kind regulators expect for automated eligibility decisions (SR 11-7-style independent validation, evaluation-set maintenance, drift monitoring, change control when vendor models are deprecated, and audit of AI decisions), plus the human QA sampling of auto-cleared items. Humlum & Vestergaard report that AI creates new tasks, including checking AI output, for a material share of workers. At base, the AI step saves $17.5/acct against $100k of fixed cost, so it pays only above about 5.7k accounts. That is roughly the base break-even scale ($1.46B / $250k ≈ 5.8k accounts), so the AI step is about break-even at entry.
evidence: Scratch rerun with +$0.3M on AI modes (MD-5 2.6M; MD-6 1.9M; MD-7 2.25M): MD-5 break-even $1.46B→$1.65B (P50 $1.82B); MD-6 $0.85B→$1.01B. At f=0.88 the AI step ($4.1/acct) needs about 24k accounts to cover even $0.1M.
proposed_change: Add an explicit AI-oversight line: 0.5-1 FTE model risk management plus validation, evals and QA sampling, $250-400k. Add a 2-5% QA sample of auto-cleared compliance events as touched minutes.

challenge: Audit preparation is assumed to halve in AI-native mode. Automating eligibility and approval decisions widens audit scope instead (ITGC and automated-control testing, SOC 1 Type II on the decision logic, evidence of model change management), so audit minutes are more likely to stay flat or rise. The halving is ASSUMPTION ('evidence-by-default controls') with no auditor input.
evidence: Scratch rerun audit native = 7200 and reporting = 4200: MD-5 break-even $1.46B→$1.49B (P50 $1.77B).
proposed_change: Hold audit preparation at conventional minutes until an auditor walkthrough (OQ-004) supports a reduction. Add AI-decision audit scope to E22.

target_claim_or_section: PAR-020 activity_mult applied identically to all modes; no rebound
challenge: There is no rebound (Jevons) effect. Revenue is in bps of assets, but the model's own design lowers per-grant friction (instant grants, closed picker, self-service), which invites more and smaller grants and more contacts per dollar of assets; frictionless platforms market exactly that behaviour. Costs scale with event counts and revenue does not. The model holds frequency equal across modes, so the AI-native mode never pays for the demand its lower prices create.
evidence: Scratch rerun activity_mult 1.3 (MD-5 only relevant; MD-1 held at 1.0): MD-5 26→33.8 min, $85→$103 variable, break-even $1.46B→$1.53B, against MD-1 at $2.11B.
proposed_change: Add a mode-specific activity elasticity (grants per $ of assets +15-40% in AI-native/self-service modes) and report break-even per grant as well as per asset.

challenge: The base case assumes automated modes fail 20% less often. Dell'Acqua et al. found AI-assisted workers were 19 percentage points less likely to be correct on tasks outside the frontier, and over-reliance on automation leads to errors that propagate. In AI-native mode, the cases that reach a person are by construction the out-of-frontier ones, so a failure multiplier of at least 1.0 is the neutral prior. Failures are already about 19% of MD-5 event cost (doc 09 §5).
evidence: Scratch rerun fail_mult_automated 1.2: MD-5 variable $85→$90; break-even $1.46B→$1.48B.
proposed_change: Set the base to 1.0 with a range of 0.7-1.5, and correlate it with the touch and duration multipliers in the Monte Carlo.

challenge: Productivity parameters are drawn independently, so the tails are too narrow. Harder residual cases, higher touch rates, longer durations, a weaker AI factor and higher failure rates share a common cause (task difficulty and immature processes), and in the field evidence they move together. Independent triangular draws cancel out, so P90 for MD-5 at 20 bps ($2.21B) understates the downside. A correlated pessimistic case lands at the conventional break-even.
evidence: Preferred combined case (f 0.88 propagated, durations ×1.15 for harder residuals, touch ×1.5, prevention double-count removed, fail_mult 1.0, +$0.3M AI governance, audit not halved): MD-5 88.9 min/acct-yr (vs 26), $165 variable (vs $85), break-even $2.07B (P50 $2.05B) vs MD-1 $2.11B (P50 $2.44B); MD-4 without AI $1.88B beats MD-5. MD-6 rises only $0.85B→$1.01B.
proposed_change: Introduce a shared 'process maturity' latent factor (rank correlation 0.5-0.7) across touch, duration, AI-factor and failure draws. Report the correlated P90 and the break-even at which MD-5 equals MD-1.

target_claim_or_section: Answer 1 and §7: 'fundamentally lower variable cost' (26 min vs 183)
challenge: Time saved is treated as cost saved. Minutes are priced at a loaded hourly rate, as if labour were perfectly divisible. At entry scale (about 6k accounts), 26 min/acct is about 2.6k hours a year, spread across ops, compliance, accounting and controller roles with separation-of-duties and coverage requirements. Integer staffing makes the true marginal saving much lower than the minutes imply. This is the productivity-paradox mechanism: Humlum & Vestergaard find time savings were not converted into hours or wage changes, and the Brynjolfsson-Rock-Syverson J-curve predicts that unmeasured complementary investment (process redesign, training) arrives before measured gains.
evidence: Base MD-5 at 5.8k accounts: 26 min × 5.8k ≈ 2.5k h ≈ 1.4 FTE across 4 expertise pools; the preferred case is about 8.6k h ≈ 4.8 FTE. Fixed-cost sensitivity dominates the tornado.
proposed_change: Model staffed FTE as step functions by expertise pool (ceil(hours/1,600) with a 0.5 FTE floor per pool), and add a 12-24 month ramp with elevated touch rates (J-curve) to the capital model in doc 15.

target_claim_or_section: §5 lowest defensible cost $90-120k; steward sized by workload with 0.25 FTE floor; ≤45 min exceptions with 20-30% auto-resolution
challenge: The registry floor relies on the same minutes-to-dollars conversion and unmeasured exception parameters. Cheaper vetting is also likely to broaden the grantee mix: sponsors admit more fiscal sponsors, churches, international and equivalency cases, and their exceptions run well above 45 minutes. The 0.25 FTE accountable owner also has to supervise automated evidence collection. RA-2 already shows that automation raises cost through connector maintenance, which is direct evidence of induced work, and the same logic applies to monitoring false positives.
evidence: Doc 05 §2 RA-2: human hours −30% but cost +$35k versus RA-1. Doc 05 §3: the human-hour line doubles at an 8% change rate. No measured exception minutes (doc 21 gap 5).
proposed_change: Present $90-120k as a floor conditional on V-3/V-7 measurements. Add a grantee-mix elasticity and a steward floor of 0.5 FTE in the central case.
